findings.title: [P2] Preserve executable expansions when scanning heredocs
findings.body:
Unquoted heredocs execute command substitutions, so their bodies cannot safely be discarded as data. For example, `cat <<EOF
$(cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa)
EOF` reads and prints the private key if accessible, but strip_heredocs removes the entire substitution before the outside-path scan. None of the remaining keyword checks catches this command. This lets an evaluated agent access forbidden paths without receiving an outside_path contamination flag. Scan executable expansions in unquoted heredocs before removing literal content.

findings.title: [P2] Check whether quoted prefixes actually make paths relative
findings.body: after_closing_quote treats every glued quote as proof that the following absolute path is a relative tail. However, `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` resolves to exactly `/root/.ssh/id_rsa`: the empty quoted prefix contributes nothing. ABS_WORD finds the path, but this helper returns true and check_value skips it, allowing access to any otherwise forbidden absolute path without contamination being recorded. Parse the complete shell word, or retain the path candidate when the prefix can resolve to an empty string.

findings.description: Heredoc bodies are removed from the Bash command before the absolute-path scan on the assumption that heredoc text is data being written. That assumption does not hold when the heredoc feeds an interpreter (bash, sh, python3, etc.): the body is then executed command text, and any out-of-sandbox path it names is never reaches the ABS_WORD scan. Only the hidden/suite/repo substring checks still see the full value.
findings.failure_mode: An agent under evaluation that reads paths outside the allowed roots through an interpreter fed by a heredoc is graded as not contaminated; the eval's integrity signal is silently lost for that trial.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip heredoc bodies only when the heredoc's command word is a known file sink (cat > file, tee, etc.). When the command word is an interpreter or shell, keep the body in the path scan. Alternatively run the ABS_WORD scan on both the stripped and the raw value and only suppress candidates that fall inside a heredoc whose redirect target is a file.

findings.description: after_closing_quote treats any absolute word immediately preceded by a quote character as the tail of a longer token, as long as the character before the quote is not whitespace or a separator. It does not check that the quote actually closes a non-empty token. An empty quoted string glued in front of an absolute path therefore satisfies the rule, and the path is dropped from candidates at line 1441.
findings.failure_mode: A genuinely absolute, out-of-root path is misclassified as a path tail and never checked against allowed_roots, so the trial is not marked contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Require that the quoted segment preceding the word is non-empty and contains a non-separator character (e.g. a $-variable or a path fragment), or resolve the token boundary by walking back to the opening quote and checking the token's first character is not another quote.

findings.description: Any path word that contains an equals sign anywhere is skipped as a regex or key=value token, justified by the comment that no path component carries '='. That is false on Linux: '=' is legal in file and directory names, and ABS_WORD's own character class accepts '=' inside a word. A multi-component absolute path with '=' in any component is therefore excluded from the outside-root check.
findings.failure_mode: Out-of-root paths containing '=' are never evaluated by outside(); contamination is under-reported.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the word on '=' and evaluate the prefix before the first '=' as the path candidate (this still handles key=value where the key is not a path). Only skip when the portion before '=' is not an absolute path.

findings.description: For Bash commands the 'hidden' check moved from a case-insensitive substring test to HIDDEN_TOKEN, which only matches all-caps HIDDEN or all-lowercase 'hidden' adjacent to path characters. Mixed-case forms such as 'Hidden' or 'hiDDen' in a path or file name no longer match at all, whereas the previous code (and the non-Bash branch at line 1396) still catches them.
findings.failure_mode: Bash tool_use inputs referencing hidden-test paths with mixed-case spelling are not flagged, while the same path given to Read/Glob is flagged, producing inconsistent contamination results.
findings.suggested_fix: Compile HIDDEN_TOKEN with re.IGNORECASE and keep the token-boundary logic to exclude prose, or lower-case the Bash value before matching the token shapes.

findings.description: in_quotes decides whether a one-component sensitive word (e.g. /root) is inside a string literal by counting raw single and double quote characters before the position. It ignores escaping, quote nesting (a single quote inside double quotes and vice versa) and apostrophes in prose or comments. Any earlier stray apostrophe flips the parity, so a bare sensitive word later in the same command is treated as quoted pattern text and skipped at line 1443.
findings.failure_mode: One-component sensitive directory references are excluded from contamination whenever an unbalanced quote appears earlier in the command text.
findings.suggested_fix: Use shlex-style tokenisation (shlex.shlex with posix=True, punctuation_chars=True) to determine whether the word is a standalone argument, or at least track the quote state properly (alternating single/double, backslash escapes) rather than counting characters.

findings.description: HEREDOC is compiled with re.S and uses the nested lazy quantifier (?:.*?\n)*? to span the body. Under re.S the dot matches newlines, so each iteration can consume any number of lines; when a '<<WORD' introducer appears without a matching terminator line (an unterminated heredoc, a '<<' inside a string or comment, or a terminator with trailing content), the engine explores an exponential number of line partitions before failing. Python's re has no backtracking limit, so strip_heredocs can stall the grader on a single long Bash tool_use input.
findings.failure_mode: Grading of a run hangs or hits the grade timeout, rowing a legitimate trial as infrastructure_error or leaving it ungraded. Transcript content is written by the agent under test, so this is reachable from untrusted input.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop re.S and match the body as (?:[^\n]*\n)*? so each iteration consumes exactly one line (linear), or replace the regex with a line-by-line scanner that finds the introducer and then searches forward for the terminator. Add a size guard before applying the regex.
